title: First black band at the auditorium; Copeland, Izel and Desvigne
summary: Hired by Walter Hubbard for Carnival, before Duke Ellington; Thomas Copeland's illness, Izel Robinson and Sidney Desvigne.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Where did you play? I said...

He was my husband's band. It was the first band, colored band, played at the auditorium. Oh, I see. That was the... During a carnival. He was hired by... It's so hard, we were in between, I just stopped up. He was hired by Walter Hubbard. You know, he used to work for all them people, you know, that had to call for parades. And... Paran. I said Uncle Richard. And... Thomas Copeland. Izel and all that. And I believe he had that boy, Moran Whitton, that time. And after he played there, that's where Duke Ellington came in and played there. There was the second band played at the auditorium. Your daddy was the first one. Played at that auditorium. What's happened to Thomas Copeland? And all that, none of that, never what, never right, none of that. What happened to Thomas Copeland? Well, he died, you know. No, I didn't know. Yeah, he took very sick. And he lost, his wife went down in a canal in an automobile, you know. And that car made a fake on him. And he took sick from that. And then he had, he was at the hospital and they say he had broke a bottle or something. And tried to commit suicide, cut his wrist. But he got all right a little bit. He never was so, you remember him. Yeah. But he was saying how he was so glad to meet you, you know. And... Cause you met him somewhere you was playing, I think. Yeah. And so anyhow, he got come all right. And then after that he died. He used to wait for the slaughterhouse. Yeah. But he killed all them cattle, you know. That's the cattle.
Was he about your husband's age?

Who, Thomas Copeland? Yeah. I think he might have been a little younger, no. He might have been a little younger, you know. Not too much. I think Izel, you know, we used to call him Ogoose. I think he was about in his age, you know. Maybe he was a little old, I don't know. Maybe just his belt or something, you know. But, uh, there was all, there was all with the band. He'd give that up a good while ago, this fellow Izel Robinson. And he was like, what we call Ogoose, you know. I saw him. Cause he had a, I think he had a stroke and thing. He had been right sick. He had given up a good volume. But anyway, to tell you, uh, by all them playing there, you never heard nothing of that, you know. And when he put that little write up for my niece's husband in there. Well, I don't know who gave that record. Cause, uh, they didn't mention too much at all was the foundation of him playing. Cause he did all bodies first horn and everything. And he was the one that started them out. And Richard also first started out with, he played a little bit, but not too much with no band. Cause all first took him when he had Sidney Daysby in. Sidney Daysby in was his trumpet player. He died not too long, you know. Cause at least send me words, you know. Sidney Daysby. Was he still playing in California?
No, I think he had a restaurant out there. Oh yeah.

Well anyway, he, uh, was our neighbor one time. He owned a little house right down St. Philip. But, uh, I don't know why, but, uh, I guess all got kind of disgusted when that man, I'll never forget that. The associate, uh, do so much about it. Not even like in a, a praise, you know, he didn't put nothing about it or nothing. And he'd get right smarter pictures. After that, somebody else had came through and said, you know, that, uh, he could get the pictures back. But he didn't know, I don't know. He gave a lot of pictures he had at home, but different boys, you know. Sidney Vinn, I don't know if you knew Sidney Vinn. I've heard of him.
